title: NCPatcher extraction manifest
description: What `ncpatcher rom extract` wrote into a directory, and how. It exists because a directory of loose binaries cannot answer two questions about itself: which layout its file names follow, and what form each overlay was stored in. `rom pack` reads it to put the original form back; any other tool reading such a directory can read it for the same reason.

rom.description: File name of the ROM this came out of. Informational: a directory is packed back into whatever ROM the caller names, not into this one.

code-only.description: True when `--code-only` was used, so the directory holds the header, the ARM binaries, the overlay tables and the overlays and nothing else. A directory like that is not one a tool can read back as a whole ROM.

decompressed-overlays.description: True when `--decompress-overlays` was used. Per-overlay detail is in `overlays`; this is the summary.

layout.description: The DirLayout the extraction used, field by field, so a reader does not have to guess which extractor wrote the directory. These are the names actually used, which a project may have overridden rather than taken from a preset.

overlay9-name.description: `{id}` is the overlay number; `{id:4}` pads it to four digits.

data-dir.description: Directory the NitroFS tree was written below, at the paths the ROM names.

overlays.description: One record per overlay, carrying what the ROM's own table said whatever the emitted table says. This is the half of the answer the directory cannot hold: once an overlay has been unpacked and its flag cleared, nothing on disk remembers that the ROM had it compressed, and a repack that guessed would be guessing about whether the console can boot.

proc.description: Which processor's overlay table this row belongs to.

id.description: The overlay number, which is also its index in that table.

stored.description: `as-in-rom` means the file on disk is byte for byte what the ROM held, compression and all. `raw` means the extraction decompressed it and cleared the compression flag in the emitted overlay table to match; the two always move together, because decompressed bytes under a row still claiming a compressed size is the one combination that produces a ROM that hangs.

rom-flags.description: The flags byte the ROM's own overlay table row carried, as a hexadecimal string. Bit 0 is compressed, bit 1 is authenticated (GBATEK). Restored by `rom pack` when `stored` is `raw`.

rom-compressed-size.description: The compressed size the ROM's own row carried. Recorded for reference; a repack recomputes it, since recompressing does not have to reproduce the original stream byte for byte.
